catalog_quote: First, Kagoshima Japanese permits only two accentual (or tonal) patterns, traditionally called A and B (Hirayama 1951). Tone A involves a pitch fall towards the end of the word, with only the penultimate syllable high-toned. Tone B, on the other hand, does not involve an abrupt pitch fall and keeps only the final syllable high- toned. ... (1) ka.NA.da 'Canada', DOI.tu 'Germany', IN.do 'India', HA.wai 'Hawaii', su.WEE.den 'Sweden' (2) a.me.ri.KA 'America', i.gi.ri.SU 'England, Britain', hu.ran.SU 'France' ... A second salient feature of Kagoshima Japanese is that its prosodic system is based on the syllable rather than the mora ... The loci of high tone in (1), for example, can be generalized by stating 'find the second syllable from the end of the word and keep it high-toned.' ... Kagoshima Japanese is not only a 'syllable-counting' dialect; the tone bearing unit is also the syllable ra…

tone_statements.citation: Bučar Shigemori, Lia Saki & Yuki Asano. 2025. Tonal sound change in Kagoshima Japanese: Production of monosyllabic words. Proceedings of the Third International Conference on Tone and Intonation (TAI 2025), 45-49. doi:10.21437/TAI.2025-10.
tone_statements.quote: KJ and TJ are both lexical pitch accent languages … KJ permits only two accent patterns, traditionally called Type A and Type B. In polisyllabic words that belong to Type A, the penultimate syllable has a high pitch peak followed by a fall and the last syllable has a low pitch. In words that belong to Type B, only the last syllable has a high pitch. If particles are attached to the word within the same accentual phrase, the position of the pitch peak moves with it to align with the end of the accentual phrase boundary.
tone_statements.locator: p. 45, Abstract and sec. 1.1 'Lexical pitch accent in KJ and TJ'
tone_statements.summary: Lexical pitch accent with two word patterns: Type A (high peak on the penult, then a fall) and Type B (high on the final syllable), aligned to the phrase end; the young merge them in monosyllables.

tone_statements.citation: Taki, Ryuichi (髙城隆一). 2020. 鹿児島県大隅半島内之浦方言における二型アクセントの痕跡 [Traces of a two-pattern accent system in the Uchinoura dialect of Kagoshima Japanese]. 東京大学言語学論集 (Tokyo University Linguistic Papers, TULIP) 42: 267-282. doi:10.15083/00079921, hdl:2261/00079921.
tone_statements.quote: …内之浦方言のアクセント体系を記述し、二型アクセントの痕跡が今なお残存することを指摘する。拡張語を 2 つ以上使用した文中での名詞の発音を観察すると、ある話者の発音では鹿児島市方言の二型アクセントと類似する、対立する 2 種類のアクセント型が現れる … 拡張語を単独で発音した際にはアクセント型の対立が見られない別の話者も、文中での発音においては 2 種類のアクセント型が比較的安定して現れることが明らかになった。 … つまり、A 型は「次末音節のみが高い型」であり、B 型と X 型は「最終音節のみが高い型（最終音節内での下降の有無は問わない）」であると捉えることができる。 … これを踏まえて、本稿では内之浦方言の A 型を「下降型」、B 型を「非下降型」と解釈する。
tone_statements.translation: …describe the accent system of the Uchinoura dialect and show that traces of a two-pattern accent remain. In sentences with two or more extended words, one speaker's nouns show two contrasting accent types like the Kagoshima-city two-pattern accent … another speaker, with no accent-type contrast on isolated extended words, also shows two accent types fairly stably in sentences. … That is, Type A is 'only the penultimate syllable high' and Types B and X 'only the final syllable high (fall inside it or not)'. … On this basis Uchinoura Type A is read as 'falling', Type B as 'non-falling'.
tone_statements.locator: p. 267 (要旨) + pp. 276-277 (§4.1 拡張語単独での発音)
tone_statements.summary: Uchinoura dialect: two accent patterns over word+clitics, A (penultimate syllable high, falling) vs B (final syllable high); they vary freely in isolation and contrast only in sentence context.

tone_statements.citation: Kodama, Nozomi (児玉望). 2005. 鹿児島タイプ二型アクセントの音調句 [Prosodic sandhi and its domain in a two-tone (two-pattern) accent system of the Kagoshima type]. ありあけ: 熊本大学言語学論集 (Ariake: Kumamoto University linguistic papers) 4: 281-307.
tone_statements.quote: 鹿児島市方言のアクセントが、アクセント単位の音節数にかかわらず二つの型のいずれかの形をとるいわゆる二型アクセントのタイプであることは、平山輝男(1936)をはじめとして … よく知られた事実である。 … 二音節以上の長さのアクセント単位では、 A型では次末音節が高く末音節が低く、 B型では末音節が高い。単音節のアクセント単位でも A型は下降調、 B型は高平の二つの音調が区別される。体言に助詞がついたもの、用言の活用した形はいずれも語葉ごとに同じ型になり、また、 lアクセント単位となる複合語は原則として最初の成分の型を保持する。 … 26. 鹿児島方言アクセントの分析 A型アクセント単位 ]0/:末音節の前に下げ核 B型アクセント単位 。]/:末音節の後に下げ核 句音調 {*[・:句の最初の下げ核の直前に上げ核
tone_statements.translation: That Kagoshima City accent is the so-called two-pattern type, a unit taking one of two patterns whatever its syllable count, is well known since Hirayama (1936) … In units of two or more syllables Type A has penult high, final low; Type B final high. In monosyllables too two tones are distinguished, A falling, B high level. Noun+particle and inflected forms keep one type per lexeme; a one-unit compound keeps its first member's type. … (26) Kagoshima accent: A unit ]O/: lowering kernel before the final syllable; B unit O]/: after it; phrase tone {*[: raising kernel just before the 1st lowering.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 283-284, sec. 2 二型アクセントの音韻解釈と句音調 (before and after exx. 5-6), and p. 291, ex. (26) 鹿児島方言アクセントの分析
tone_statements.summary: Two-pattern pitch accent: each accent unit, of any length, is Type A (fall before the final syllable; monosyllable falling) or Type B (final high, fall after it); a phrasal rise precedes the 1st fall.

tone_statements.citation: Ishihara, Shunichi. 1998. An acoustic-phonetic description of word tone in Kagoshima Japanese. Proceedings of the 5th International Conference on Spoken Language Processing (ICSLP 1998, Sydney), paper 0628. doi:10.21437/ICSLP.1998-115.
tone_statements.quote: KJ shows two different surface pitch patterns, (L)0HL and (L)0H. In the former pattern, only the penultimate syllable of a word has a high pitch and every other syllable has a low pitch, and in the latter pattern, only the last syllable of a word has a high pitch and every other syllable before it has a low pitch. Therefore, KJ has often been referred to … as a typical example having only two accentual classes: type A and type B, respectively. … An alternative analysis (e.g. Hayata 1977) is that … words fall into one of two distinctive melody classes (LHL and LH).
tone_statements.locator: p. 1 of the paper (proceedings pages unnumbered), sec. 1 Introduction
tone_statements.summary: Two word-level pitch patterns: type A (L)0HL, high on the penult, vs type B (L)0H, high on the final syllable; whether this is lexical accent or two word melodies is left open; F0 study, 2 speakers.
